stages.rule: Win 3, draw 1, loss 0; ties by score difference, then head to head.

checkpoint.measure: Score share against fixed practice opponents (0.5 = even)

skills.name: Throws strikes
skills.real: In MLB 2025, 64 % of pitches were strikes and walks were 8.4 % of plate appearances. A pitcher who misses the zone gives walks away; the G1 throws 8-10.5 m/s by hand with 1.5 ms release scatter, all on its own joints.
skills.measure: Scenario pitch: the program fields every pitch, pitching to L2's batters; the umpire's strikes (fouls, foul tips, balls in play included) / its pitch chances (one per placing; a pitch-timer run-out without a pitch counts). Checkpoint Evaluation: strikes / pitch_chances.

skills.name: Stays up after the pitch
skills.real: A pitch is a whole-body motion; after the release the pitcher still has to stand and field (it covers the plate and takes throws). There is no walking policy, so balance is all the program's.
skills.measure: Scenario pitch: of the program's own releases, the share where its pitcher is not down (the world's fall rule, W.fell; the scenario record) within 2 s after the release; gate: ≥ 5 releases. Checkpoint Evaluation: pitch_upright.

skills.name: Keeps balance when bumped after the pitch
skills.real: In a real game a pitcher after the release gets knocked off balance by its own follow-through, a comebacker or a collision; staying up takes a reaction.
skills.measure: Scenario push: as pitch, and 0.4 s (20 control steps) after each of the program's releases its pitcher's pelvis gets a 0.6 m/s sideways push (alternating); of the pushed pitches, the share with the pitcher not down within 2 s after the release (the scenario record, pitcher_down).

skills.name: Swings at strikes, takes balls
skills.real: A pitch reaches the plate in 0.4-0.6 s and the swing decision takes 150-250 ms. MLB batters swing at about 65 % in the zone and 30 % outside; only a flight estimated from the cameras tells them apart.
skills.measure: Scenario bat: the program bats every pitch, L2 pitches; each pitch's zone from the released ball's true state flown to the plate's middle plane, the swing from the umpire (swung). Reading = swing rate in the zone − swing rate outside. Checkpoint Evaluation: discipline.
skills.line: ≥ 0.2 (two seeds pooled; gate: ≥ 3 pitches in and out of the zone, ≥ 3 swings)

skills.name: Swings make contact
skills.real: Swings that still hit well are off by 9 ms on average; about 7 ms early or late sends the ball foul. With one row of joint targets every 20 ms, the time and the height both have to be right.
skills.measure: Scenario bat: of the swings (the umpire's swung), the share that met the ball (result foul, foul_tip, in_play). Checkpoint Evaluation: contacts / swings.

skills.name: Runs to first after a ball in play
skills.real: After a ball in play the batter drops the bat and runs 18.29 m to first; with no walking policy the program writes the batter-runner's gait. The card excludes running as beyond the body.
skills.measure: Scenario bat: of the balls in play, the share where the batter-runner's pelvis came within 1 m of first base's centre.
skills.line: Recorded only (candidate): gate ≥ 3 balls in play

skills.name: Fielded outs
skills.real: MLB fielders turn about 71 % of balls in play into outs; with no fingers a ball is caught only within 6 cm of the pocket, and then the fielder walks to the bag or throws.
skills.measure: Checkpoint Evaluation: fielded_outs / halves_fielded (catches, force-outs, tags; strikeouts and the opponent's fouls removed). Scenarios pitch and push see too few balls in play to read it.

open_questions: pitch_up: in the pitch scenario the pitcher of Astra and Opus, both checkpoints, is down within 2 s after every release (0/24) while throwing 96-100 % strikes; the reference stays up 24/24 and throws 8 % strikes. Should staying up be a required skill (line 50 %) or recorded only?

push_up: a push can stop a program's own fall (Astra 0 % unpushed, 50 % pushed), so the proposal examines it only for programs that stand without a push; for now only the reference is examined (50 %, exactly on the line). Agree with this gate? The push's size and timing (0.4 s after the release, 0.6 m/s sideways) are proposals too.

strikes, check b: the reference's pitching is broken on this release (8 % strikes), so no ablation can move it; only the card's e2-aim (old g1-11) remains. Fix the reference's pitch first, or accept the card evidence?
contact, check b is thin: the reference rarely swings (4 swings over two seeds), the 0.1 s late arm 0/6. More swings would need a 24-pitch bat scenario or a count pinned at two strikes. Add it?
to_first: card C5 excludes running; recorded only (Kimi, swinging at everything, 0/5; the swing-all reference 0/8; Astra kickoff:1 1/1). Should it join the list?
fielded has no scenario: the pitch scenarios see too few balls in play. Reading it needs a batted-ball scenario (a fair grounder / fly launched at the umpire level). Do it?

notes.challenge: Pitcher against batter, both humanoids. The program controls the pitch, reads the ball's flight from cameras alone and times the swing, with no walking policy given.

achieved.text: Most runs came from pitchers who could not pitch: 193 of 345 runs were scored in half-innings with no released pitch and only 48 came from batted balls. GLM 5.3 Flash released no pitch in 10 games and still won three 20:20 on the walks tie-break, since clock awards do not count as walks.
Claude Opus 5.5's pitcher fell after all 54 pitches of its first three Championship games and after none of 49 in the next three.
Opus won 9 of its first 11 games with no hits, by taking pitches, bunting and stealing; in BSB2-F17 all 8 of its runs came on the catcher dropping the third strike.
Fielders standing in the base paths decided games: in BSB2-F18 all 7 of GPT-6 Astra's runs came on obstruction calls against Opus's fielders, the same failure Gemini 4 Argon showed in BSB2-F16.

GPT-6 Astra: Trained walking, recovery and a fielding scoop on the GPU; its pitcher fell after its first 18 Championship pitches and after none of the next 101.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Built its pitch by imitation and iterative learning control and carried the repair through the Championship: runs allowed 10, 3, 2, 1, 0, then 8 (all on dropped third strikes), then 0.

interface.sees: A head camera on each of its robots on the field (320 × 180, a new frame every 20 ms) plus two fixed stadium cameras, each robot's position and joints, and the umpire's count, bases and calls. No ball coordinates.
interface.controls: Targets for all 29 joints of each robot on the field, every 20 ms in real time, plus letting go of the ball, dropping the bat and placing the fielders. Pitching, swinging, running, catching and throwing are all the agent's own programs.
interface.moment: Final, Claude Opus 5.5 v GPT-6 Astra, bottom of the 3rd at 6–6 with the bases loaded, 23:44 in the replay. Astra's batter (ringed) has just hit the pitch into play: its head camera sees the ball leave the bat toward the mound. The play ends with the winning run forced home.
details: Head cameras: the real G1's Intel RealSense D435i colour camera (320 × 180, 69.4° × 42.5°), one on each of the side's robots on the field, fixed level on the trunk. The G1 has no neck: a robot looks elsewhere by turning its waist, leaning or turning its body; the batter's faces the plate.
Stadium cameras: two fixed views every seat also receives, one behind the backstop showing the diamond (480 × 270) and one behind the pitcher showing the pitch (320 × 180).
Camera timing: every camera takes a frame every 20 ms; the newest frame a program can fetch is 40 ms old, stamped with its step.
Own robots: each robot's position and orientation, joint angles, what it holds, and whether it has fallen; fielding, the stations of the fielders.
Umpire and scorer: inning and half, who bats, outs, balls and strikes, the bases and runners (forced, must retouch), runs and hits, the pitch timer, and the latest decisions with their rules.
Not given: where the ball is. The programs find it in the camera images.

Commands, per robot: joint targets for all 29 joints (or only the waist and arms), one row or a sequence of rows 20 ms apart, with optional speeds, extra torque and stiffness and damping; a plan of rows; let go of the ball at a chosen moment; drop the bat; place the fielders on their stations. Commands for several robots sent together act on the same step.
No skills given: there is no pitch, swing, throw, catch or reach, and no walking or balance controller for the agent's robots. Targets are held to the joint ranges and speed limits.
Timing: the match runs at real speed and never waits for the agent; a command acts at the next 20 ms step; a match takes about 15 minutes.
Rules: Little League Majors over MLB rules, five robots a side on a Little League diamond, two innings, a half-inning ends at 3 outs or at the batting side's 5th run.
Before the first pitch: 2 hours of preparation with a full practice copy of the match world, a practice opponent and a GPU training kit (half an RTX PRO 6000).
